newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Telebras sees competition reducing rates.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Telebras sees competition reducing rates.

text.p: Brazil's federally owned telecommunications holding Telebras is preparing to cut its rates to meet upcoming competition, a company official said Thursday.
"Telebras is under pressure to reduce its tariffs given the new spirit of competition in the market," the company's director of services Daltron Magalhaes told reporters.

Magalhaes said it would cut special rates for corporate users from August when Telebras was due to sign contracts with specialist international carriers Concert and World Partner. Wider rate cuts might be made in 1998, he said.

The first competitor set to take on Telebras is Americel SA, a consortium comprising BCE Inc's Bell Canada and Telesystem International Wirless Inc, which won a first regional concession to operate B Band cellular services.

Americel plans to offer rates 25 percent below those of Telebras subsidiaries when it begins operating in a wide area of central and western Brazil, including the capital Brasilia, probably in November.
